comment: Provider spending (FIRECRAWL_PI_SPEC.md §10, §14, §15, §28.3; PI_BUDGET_POLICY_FILE). The residential proxy has the owner's approved cap of 1000000 micro-USD a day and 2000000 a month (2026-10-15), kept low so its use can be measured: the residential route answers a block of the home connection, never volume. LLM extraction has an approved $20 monthly cap (2026-10-15), with no LLM-specific daily cap and, since 2026-10-17, no shared daily cap across the paid categories (the Anthropic credits are promotional); each paid category keeps its own caps. A shared daily cap set later counts only the reservations made while it is set. A call to claude-sonnet-5-5 (the Agent's model, which reads up to 150000 input tokens in one call so a page's decision is never merged from parts) reserves 1290000 micro-USD for a short page and up to about 2800000 for a full one while it runs; it is streamed and runs to its end even when its caller's deadline passes, so it settles at its usage; only a stream cut by the network, ended by an error event or missing its final usage, or a call in flight when the service stops, keeps its reservation as uncertain (the status lists these). Parser and enhanced retrieval caps remain zero; PI_PAID_DISPATCH_ENABLED must also be true before a paid provider is called. Amounts are integers: micro-USD (1e-6 USD) or parser credits. A model or parser the policy does not list is refused; one without a rate card in effect is refused (fail closed). Fixture providers are unpaid and draw on their own categories, so the accounting runs end to end without money.

rateCards.subject: serper-google
rateCards.source: https://serper.dev: existing trial credits; POST /search, num=10, one credit. Allocation fixed at the 2443-credit account balance observed 2026-10-15; no purchases or reload.

rateCards.subject: brave-web
rateCards.source: https://api-dashboard.search.brave.com/documentation/guides/rate-limiting, observed 2026-10-17: quota and billing count successful requests; the account plan's price per request is not recorded, so a request is counted and its money left unknown

rateCards.subject: exa-search
rateCards.source: https://exa.ai/docs/admin/pricing.md, observed 2026-10-17: auto search $7 per 1,000 requests including 10 results, $1 per 1,000 results above 10, contents $1 per 1,000 pages per content type; whether highlights requested on /search are billed at the contents rate is not stated, so the reservation is the larger reading for 20 results with highlights ($0.017 + $0.020); each answer's costDollars.total settles it

rateCards.subject: deepseek-search
rateCards.source: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/search/, observed 2026-10-17: $0.00075 per successful search that returns results; an empty or failed search is not charged

rateCards.subject: tavily-search
rateCards.source: https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/api-credits, observed 2026-10-17: an advanced search costs two credits; each answer's usage.credits settles it

rateCards.subject: context7-docs
rateCards.source: https://context7.com/docs/search-api, observed 2026-10-17: one request per library scope; the plan's price per request is not recorded, so a request is counted and its money left unknown

rateCards.subject: ref-context
rateCards.source: https://docs.ref.tools/usage/credits, observed 2026-10-17: a search and a read each cost one credit from the account's shared pool; no balance API is documented

rateCards.subject: jev-1.14
rateCards.source: https://openrouter.ai/typesafe/jev-1.14, observed 2026-10-17: $0.042 per million input tokens, output free; an answer's usage.cost, when present, settles it

rateCards.subject: claude-sonnet-5-5
rateCards.source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing, observed 2026-10-17: base input $2, cache hit $0.10, 5-minute cache write $2.50, output $10 per MTok, one rate across the whole 1M context window (only Haiku 5.5 has a long-prompt rate); no cache_control is sent, so nothing is written to the cache

rateCards.subject: claude-haiku-5-5
rateCards.source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing, observed 2026-10-17: the rate card for prompts up to 100,000 tokens (input $0.10, cache hit $0.01, 5-minute cache write $0.125, output $0.50 per MTok); extraction input is capped at 32,000 estimated tokens per call, which keeps an ordinary page far below the 100,000-token threshold of the higher rate card; the cap is an estimate, not a bound (text heavy in emoji or rare scripts tokenises at several tokens per character), every call logs its reported prompt_tokens, and a prompt over the threshold would be priced below the higher card
